p: It’s a great question. I unfortunately cannot speak to my role but I do know that it is very much the Mayor’s intention that New Yorkers not just feel that their city if more affordable under the Mamdani Administration but feel celebrated as a city and feel that we can host the world successfully and that folks really across the world understand that New York is the best city in the world. And so, very much the intention is to continue that work without being able to say with certainty exactly what shape it will take for now but I do think this is an exciting opportunity to build out what that could look like.
Thank you so much for your time.

I want to recognize Council Member Avilés for joining us and piggyback on Council Member Riley’s questions around security. I know the state secured funding for federal counter drone efforts specific to the World Cup and curious how the Czar and the Administration is coordinating with State Police, MTA Police and then of course Port Authority on the security planning.

Absolutely. Uhm, PD, FDNY, and NJSPD, Port Authority and others have all been in really close coordination around transit, mobility and safety insecurity uhm as far as the Drone program. And I’ll just say there’s working groups and the conversations have been ongoing for the past two years. So, feeling very confident about both the preparedness and then also preparation for contingency and far as specifics on the Drone program, that is something we can get back about.
And does the city have a plan to increase the security budget around the World Cup independent from these other efforts?
That is something I can get back to you on.
Sounds good. I want to acknowledge Council Member Shanel Thomas-Henry to ask any questions she may have.

Thank you. Thank you Chair. I have a couple. So, I represent the 21st Council District where the Queens Fair Zone will be. So, my first question is, who is managing that experience? Is it the USTA, is it EDC? Who will be responsible for everything from hiring, programming and the like?
That would be the FIFA Host Committee.
And is there a cost for that event?
Well, as in for New Yorkers to attend?
Yes.
Uhm, we are having conversations with the Host Committee to make sure that the event is as affordable and accessible as possible to every New Yorker.

Okay and do we have any idea how those tickets would be distributed? Because oftentimes when they are - like, just from

experience, we have the U.S. open every year. Usually when those tickets are open, a lot of our residents who literally live walking distance, miss out. So, is there anything being put in place to make sure that residents that are like surrounding this area have either first access or to those tickets?

We are negotiating all of the details and it’s not locked yet but very much the intention is affordability, accessibility and obviously tourists going to the five boroughs but also New Yorkers in the five boroughs being able to take advantage of it, which is why we’re very excited that one of the major events is going to be in Queens. So, very much something we’re working on. It’s a priority and can get back to you on the details, which we hope to have quite soon.
And is FIFA also responsible for doing the hiring for that event? And if so, do we know when that is going to start?
Yes, they are - they are hosting funding and you know contracting and so, they should be. I’m not quite sure when that will begin.

Okay, I’d like if we could have coordination with my other office because again, it’s literally in the district, in our backyard. From a transportation perspective, what is the plan for transit and traffic mitigation? Keeping in mind for the law at least a week of these events, the METS are playing at home.

Absolutely. Uhm, I can speak kind of more broadly to our transit coordination and then on the specifics of coordinating related to METS games. I know that those conversations are very much in progress and so, we can and will coordinate with your office to understand more what the nitty gritty details will be. Uhm, I think so on the overall kind of transit piece, obviously first and foremost, our goal is to move people via mass transit. We know that that is going to be either way the majority of fans reach matches and also travel throughout the city and we plan to highly, highly encourage the use of mass transit. So, transportation planning has been kind of one of our earliest and most intensive coordination areas.

We also want to ensure that we are not clogging the street with additional private vehicles where possible, because we really want to make sure that streets are moving for every day workers to get to work and school and causing as little disruption as possible. We’ve been working very closely with the Host Committee and all city and state and federal partners on transportation planning for over two years. Kind of meeting regularly with MTA, New Jersey Transit, Amtrac, Port Authority, all the partners and I’ll say New Jersey Transit is managed by the state of New Jersey and they are actively developing their plans but as far as uhm, kind of the coordination happening internally, that is very much in progress and can speak with the Committee about more details.
A recommendation would be something to consider as well. Just keep in mind that the 7 Train on a good day is overcrowded. LIR and have you guys explored possible ferry service?

Yup and I can take that very question. Uhm, so first off, we’re very proud of our ferry system of course. We’ve had two really great

milestones recently. One is we had our 50 millionth customer since the formation of the system. And then two, we announced that we reached all time records last year in terms of ridership. So, it will be part of the overall infrastructure of public transportation for the city and for presidents and visitors alike during the World Cup. The summer is our peak season, so our ferries will be out in full force throughout the entire summer. As of right now, that is our plan. Should there be other needs that arise, we will work very closely with the Czar and her team to figure out what we can do.

But keep in mind, currently we don’t have a ferry stop at this location. So, it would be put in the infras- making sure that you guys route. So, currently there’s no route to this location via the ferry service. I mean it’s accessible and it’s something that we would like to see, not just for that but permanently. So, if you guys can explore that as a transit option, it would be greatly appreciated. I want to move into small businesses, have you guys or have you recommended to FIFA to coordinate

with some of our locals like the Queens Economic Development Corporation, the Chambers of the like, to help support small businesses in the surrounding area? And by support, I mean everything from I know there were dollars uhm, slated toward marketing and branding. So, going back to Council uhm Chair Maloney’s point of, do we have opportunities for revenue generation? Like, is EDC or whomever creating something that comes from New York that we can start marketing and selling to generate revenue. We have both airports in Queens. So, as soon as someone gets off the plane, they can buy something, brand it right here in New York for our small businesses who are wanting to buy from random wholesalers knockoff merchandise. We can create a system that they’re buying it from the City of New York and expanding their business opportunities. So, is that something from a creative standpoint that you guys may have considered?

We have explored that and we also are having new conversations because in the past there were always licensees and existing retail outlets. They’ve been playing a little bit with La Guardia with small businesses and local makers but we

have some upcoming conversations to just revisit that in the next two weeks just to see how it could be physically placed in the airport.

I can definitely help with that, I just came from the airport. No, but I really want to explain upon that conversation because again, it is something that will support our small businesses. It would be revenue generating for our city and it’s a win-win opportunity that I don’t want us to lose sight of. Will the fan experience disrupt the Queens night market in any way and will there be, have you considered any additional support to those businesses that are at the Queens night market?

The fan experience currently does not disrupt the Queens night market. I can get you the exact details but I believe that’s the case and we are in coordination with the Queens night market and USTA in Flushing to kind of make sure that all of the jenga makes sense.
Okay, I just have two more questions Chair, if that’s okay. Uhm, what percentage of the media that is being spent is being spent with ethnic and community media outlets?

We’re taking a programmatic approach because it allows us to target based on the behavior of the consumer. So, we want to make sure it’s a good budget. It’s not a budget that we can just throw you know widely. So, we’re trying to target those folks who are showing intent to travel, who want to travel for big events. And then when we bring them to our website, they’re seeing all the neighborhood content and our small business content and the calendar that drives. So, we’ve got to get them to our page and then drive them deep into neighborhood guides, where those businesses are featured. That’s the way we can best track it because we also now are able to bring a tool on that will show us who came to the website, who saw the media and then we were - we’ll identify points of interest across all five boroughs. We’ll be able to see if they in fact went to those places and the only way we can do that is through programmatic buys, which really target the person based on what behavior they’re showing. So, we’re doing - we’re always open to adding to other outlets but because we’re trying to bring people in and get them disbursed, that’s the most surgical way of doing it but we haven’t - we are

only now just planning so we’re always open to more neighborhood outlets as well.

Okay and just the last thing going back to transportation, two comments in terms of traffic management because now you have two major fan fare events that are in New York. Have you had discussions with the NYPD for increased traffic management? Again, from experience we have these open every year.

Yes, uhm, thank you for your question. Absolutely uhm and those conversations have been ongoing for the past two years both in terms of traffic management but also security in general because those two events have been I believe it’s Rockefeller Center and USTA. Those events have been in the works for awhile, so those conversations are ongoing. And then we are also having kind of coordination meetings regarding other summer events and just making sure that there’s appropriate capacity to make sure that everything is safe and moving smoothly.

And would also recommend coordination with MTA because the two closest stops, 103rd and 111th are under major

construction. One of those - at least one of those you can’t even get off on one, so there’s no access. So, if that work could be expedited or worked out in some way, it would be great.
Thank you.
And final, sorry, this is my final question. The park, where residents have complete and full access unimpeded to Flushing Meadows Corona Park during this entire experience.
I can get you more details on that. I believe so but I need to get you more details.
Okay, thank you.

Thank you. I want to acknowledge we’ve been joined by Public Advocate Jumaane Williams and Council Member Banks. On the transportation theme, the 2014 Superbowl at MetLife Stadium is the most comparable recent event, mega event that the New York area has hosted and was widely seen as a logistical disappointment. So, what specifically with Transportation, so what has EDC or the Czar done to examine that event and what are we going to be doing differently this time?

Thank you. The region has definitely learned from past high demand events at

MetLife, including the Superbowl and others. New Jersey transit is led by New Jersey and they are responsible for their service planning and operations for MetLife related event travel. We have been coordinating with them together for the past two years and from the city side, our focus is making sure that New York City system, subways, buses, streets, public space management, way finding and public information are ready for surges and clearer to the public. And more specifically, NYPD is working alongside DOT to provide easy mobility for ticket holders to be transported by a bus to New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium. And so, we have kind of multimobile options and we know that at least as a beginning level of detail, a code and lane will be constructed along a dedicated route for restricted access to MTA buses only, as well as first responders and FIFA shuttles that are also planning to bring fans to the matches. So, multimodal options and then ensuring that there are contingency plans in case any of you know - any issues arise and then of course clear, multilingual communication around the whole thing.
One contingency plan, New York - sorry, New Jersey transit is expected to complete the transit way right before the tournament begins. So, do we have a contingency plan if that’s not operational?
That’s a good question. We can get back to you with that.
And are there any additional preparations that you as the Czar are making with DOT for traffic management on the New York City side?

Absolutely. We, uhm, understand that not only is the World Cup happening this summer but also a variety of other events are happening. And so, these conversations have been happening for two years and again, really want to emphasize MTA, New Jersey Transit, Port Authority, regional partners, all involved and we can absolutely kind of make sure to update the Committee on more detail around those plans, so.

One of the proposals from the mayoral administration is a five week free bus pilot during the people World Cup and from a logistical and operational standpoint, we are dealing

with so much other complexity, how feasible is it going to be to implement this systemwide free bus service during that period?

Thank you for the question. We are continuing to have conversations internally and with the Governor on what it would look like to make buses fare free and we will keep the Council updated as those conversations progress.

How does your office anticipate that this might impact New Yorkers who are relying on those buses for their regular daily commutes? Especially, when we’re already concerned about overcrowding and ridership and maintaining reliable service.

Absolutely, I can say that over the past couple of years, a top priority has really been understanding how the tourism surge will affect transit through the city and then also making sure that New Yorkers themselves do not face disruption. And we’re happy to you know after this, kind of follow up with more details as well.

Then the last question on that theme is, what would the expected revenue loss be when you know, we have this opportunity for

massive economic benefit if we were to lose that revenue from tourists.
For the bus fare. I can get back to you on that. Thank you for the question.
I want to pass to our Public Advocate to say a few words.

Thank you so much Madam Chair, appreciate it. Thank you for allowing me to give an opening statement in the middle of the hearing. Much appreciated and thank you for being here. As mentioned, my name is Jumaane Williams and I’m Public Advocate for the City of New York. I’d like to thank Chair Maloney and the Members of the Committee on Economic Development for holding this timely hearing. I just wanted to make sure some of my thoughts were on the record. New York City and much of the area, including both New York City and parts of New Jersey, is gearing up to host a significant portion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. This includes eight matches, most notably the final one July 19, 2026, which will be held at MetLife Stadium.

New York City anticipates welcoming and additional 1.2 million visitors for the event. An event so large with an unprecedented influx of national and international visitors, these games would require extensive collaboration with state and federal government partners. These visitors and events surrounding the World Cup are projected to drastically increase pressure on Port Authority, Trans, Hudson Path Trains, New Jersey Transit, and MTA subways particularly around Midtown bus tunnels. The Mamdani Administration is pushing a five week free bus pileup during the World Cup, which I think is great but the plan hinges on state approval and MTA support because no parking will be available at the stadium itself, the MTA is correlating with New Jersey Transit and Port Authority to manage increased traffic. We can easily assume also that hotel numbers will reach capacity with Time Square likely serving as the major planning zone. Furthermore, cultural institutions throughout the city such as the Whitman Museum are planning to customize events to coincide

with the tournament and many other museums, restaurants or businesses will likely do the same. Rockefeller Center will host a major fan village with additional activities at Louis Armstrong Stadium in Queens. Port Authority plans to help manage traffic flow, especially through the Midtown bus tunnel and New York City health officials have begun running drills for potential infectious disease outbreaks, including sites at La Guardia Airport. New Yorkers, particularly those with mixed status families or without legal authorization and the international tourists, should be aware that U.S. Immigration Custom Enforcement, also known as ICE, will play a “key role” in 2026 FIFA World Cup security in New York, New Jersey. ICE’s acting director Todd Lyons told the House Homeline Security Committee on February 10th that “the agency’s Homeland Security Investigations, HSI's, is “essential” for securing stadiums and protecting visitors.” The Department of Homeland Security DHS, put out a statement suggesting that “legally visiting fans had “nothing” to worry about.” Since federal law enforcement routinely secures major events like the

Superbowl, also “without conducting indiscriminate immigration sweeps.” And particularly what we saw yesterday with Columbia. I think that raises even more concern. Mayor Mamdani recently signed Executive Order 13 in a good faith effort to reinforce New York City Sanction laws and city protections to protect residents privacy and ensure continued access to city services for all New Yorkers. Regardless of immigration status, this order, a necessary response to current federal immigrant enforcement strategy, previous as from entering city owned properties. So, I'm hoping we have a plan to make sure people feel secure. I’m also very excited about the plan to try to deal with the cost of tickets. I hope we can do even more, so everyone can enjoy. And lastly, I just want to make sure that the - uh, it can be very mahacentric, which I understand but there are other parts of the city and other parts of the borough and we want to make sure we also enjoy some of the economic prosperity, including those mentioned when it come to advertisement and other ways that we can

make sure no parts of the city is left behind in enjoying what should be an awesome time. Thank you so much Madam Chair. Appreciate it and thank you for being here as well.

Thank you very much. Council Member Avilés. COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: Thank you so much CHair and thank you to the Administration for being here. Apologies if this is a question you’ve answered 12 times but uhm, such as the life of hearings. Uhm, so I guess first I’d like to you know I think cities across the country uhm, who will be hosting FIFA World Cup are obviously in various stages of planning and agreement and certainly one of the things that cities are joining in are ways to ensure that we are are safeguards around workers rights, around public safety, around impacts for vulnerable communities in particular. And so, I guess I’d love to understand about in particular, oh, I just lost my question, excuse me. I’d love to know around who in the city will be responsible for monitoring labor violations during tournament preparation and delivery. And what kind

of penalties will vendors face for wage theft as classification or unsafe working conditions.

Thank you Council Member. We are very proud to be a city that has strong labor standards and we will be ensuring those standards are met and that workers know their rights. We’re very excited to have Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice and strong advocates in the city. Strong worker protections and empowered workers who are supported by the city to know and exercise their rights benefit us all. Laws in particular like fair scheduling laws which impact the food service industry, uhm, the Safe Hotels Act, which requires panic buttons for staff and human trafficking training are two examples of the many laws that we will continue to ensure are met. COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: And so, will New York State - who is the accountability force here that will be monitoring and engaging in oversight around violations?

Uhm, the city - City Hall is coordinating and I can get back to you on exactly the levels of enforcement.

COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: And in terms of ensuring, we are - New York is a proud union town and we want to ensure that we have good union jobs and certainly pathways into those jobs, not only for this particular opportunity but ways that more of our communities can be long-lasting union workers. What kinds of models are you engaging in or developing to make sure that this is not just a one shot economic deal but that people are getting longer term union wage work?

Yeah hi, happy to take that question and thank you for the question. So again, big picture, we see this as an immense economic opportunity for the city. Uhm, not only for today but for you know as you said post World Cup as well. And so, one of the things that we are very focused on is there is going to be a large amount of businesses, large and small, who will be visiting New York City from all across the world. That is a very unique opportunity for us to go out and explain that New York City is open for business, here are the resources that are available for businesses who are considering opening up a facility in New York City and how the city can be supportive. And so, we are

aware of many different places that are bringing delegations here of businesses. For example, we know that Germans are, the French are, just to give two quick examples, and uh, we are working very closely and kind of touching up on a point of two of the other Council Members before, working very closely with the business improvement districts and also the Chambers of Commerce to making sure that when we meet with businesses who are going to be here, who are considering New York City for expansion, who will hire New York City should they come here that we’re bringing in are local partners, the BIDs, the Chambers to help sell. It’s too premature to say what type of businesses that will be here in terms of who will want to expand here but we anticipate it will be a mixture of places that will be hiring union jobs and otherwise. COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: Great, I think you know we certainly want to learn from the lessons of the past where much of these kinds of events well brought economic opportunity were rife with exploitation of individuals. So, we want to make sure that all the agreements that we are thinking through not only ensuring that we’re doing great, project labor

agreements, but also we are engaging our small businesses and providing them with real opportunity but making sure first and foremost that our workers are protected and not exploited. So, we’ll definitely continue to keep track of that. In terms of public space and I heard you and transportation, I think what we have learned from our district, we have a cruise terminal and when the giant cruise terminal comes in, our residents get pushed aside. They can’t get to work because the 5,000 new arrivals want to get on the ferry to quickly get to Manhattan. We’ve said to the city, you can create a visitor line and a resident line to make sure that residents can get access to go to work during these times. They’ve never actually implemented anything like that but we are going to have the same problem again because we are a city of 8 million people and people need to get to work. So, what kind of uhm, in addition to increasing service, the truth of the matter is, we’re probably not going to meet that. So, what kinds of programs are you thinking that we could ensure that our residents can get to where they need to go. Uhm,

because if you’re visiting for FIFA, then leave earlier but if you’re here for work, we got to support our residents first and foremost. So, are you guys thinking of any other kinds of ways to make sure that our residents can get to where they need to go?

Yeah, that’s a fantastic question. Thank you for it and specific to the cruise terminals that you mentioned before. Let me circle back at the team at EDC and we’ll follow up on that. COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: Great. In terms of public space activation and tourism, I think something we’ve also seen in other jurisdictions with mass occasions like this is people get displaced. We see serious homeless sweeps. We see displacement of local vendors. We see local businesses also getting pushed aside for whatever manner of uhm, things are coming in. So, I guess I’d love to understand like how are you planning to make sure that we are not displacing local businesses, local vendors and we’re certainly not sweeping unhoused New Yorkers to make things look pretty in a way that is undignified.

Thank you for your question. Uhm, it is our top priority to ensure that residents can celebrate the World Cup and benefit from it. And so, all of our plans are made with that in mind and uh we are very excited to share more specific plans related to activations and public space and use of public space in the coming weeks but that is absolutely top of mind for us as we are planning. COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: And in that vein, are there resources for - our public spaces are severely underfunded. In particular our park spaces. We don’t have enough workers to keep parks clean on a day to day basis. Is there going to be an infusion of funding to make sure that we have personnel to meet the demand of you know having so many new people for these events?

We are exploring different options for you know staffing amidst the infusion and the surge and can follow up with more details. COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: Is there funding, I’ve seen funding for advertisement. I have not seen funding for operational purposes for New York City staff. Like Parks cleaning staff, like the whole

workforce that we need, that is going to support this whole ecosystem and infrastructure. We see a huge advertising budget in the preliminary. I was just curious if you are intending on adding some additional resources, particularly for New York City workers who are going to need to be part of this effort.
Yes, it sounds like you’re asking about will it be an increase of budget for any of the city agencies. Is that right? COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: Yeah, yeah.

Yeah, uhm, let us circle back with you on that one. COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: Okay and lastly, in terms of the transportation, I think something we’ve seen is these giants events really depend heavily on NYPD, who also doesn’t have enough traffic agents. Is there an intention on bringing supplemental, private, traffic people to help during this time or will it be solely dependent on NYPD?

We can get back to you with more on that. Thank you. COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: Thank you and Chair, just so you know, we’re going to be submitting testimony

from Council Member Teresa Mosqueda who is a Council Member in Kings County and they’ve been doing also a lot of work on making sure that uh as a host city as well that you know that these - that this event doesn’t leave people behind and negatively affect their city and making sure that workers are absolutely protected during these things. So, we’re happy to submit it. Thank you.

Thank you very much Council Member. I echo the themes of the demands that this influx of people is going to place on our city agencies. We’ve talked about transportation, NYPD and security, I’d add sanitation to that list. Uhm, and also wanted to talk about the expected demands on our hotel economy. So, we have slowed hotel development in recent years. How do we expect hotels to be utilized during the Cup?

I think one of our strong points as a destination that we talk about often is our diversity of product and our diversity of hotel experiences. So, we are promoting all of our hotels. We are obviously featuring the fan zones and the anchor points but we understand that there is a wide variety of consumer and fan coming here hopefully.

Uhm, but also a wide variety of products available. So, we know that consumers are looking for affordable options. They exist all throughout the five boroughs. So, that’s how we’re promoting the offering.
Is there concern that predicted elevated hotel pricing during the World Cup will displace traditional summer tourists who traditionally come to New York during that period?

In July and August, we typically do a lot of our programming in July and August. Certainly we have a tourist coming here but it isn’t the peak season. So, we will have to monitor things as it gets a little bit closer but we don’t feel that that's an immediate danger.

One other point I want to raise is the federal travel ban, which I mentioned in my opening statement of 39 countries, including many of the teams that are participating. How does the city account for the potential impact of those user restrictions and immigration enforcement concerns on attendance projections and the broader tourism environment.

And I also wonder if you’ve had any communication with the federal government regarding the travel ban and the World Cup.

Thank you. We are very much aware of concerns about potential, both federal enforcement activity and the impact of the travel ban during the World Cup. Really our top priority is the safety of everyone in New York City, residents, workers and visitors alike. You know whether you were born here or not and so, the administration is in touch with the federal government and all relevant partners to ensure safety for all attendees of the World Cup. From our internal perspective, we will continue to focus on really clear and multilingual communication, coordination with our partners and ensuring that public safety operations are centered on keeping people safe and maintaining trust across communities.
Thank you. Council Member Banks, if you’d like to ask a few questions.

Thank you Chair and congratulations for this Committee hearing. Uh, with the proposed or projected $3.3 billion regional economic impact that was put forward by the New York New Jersey Host Committee. What I wanted to know was

EDC able to independently validate these numbers and if so, what sectors of the business area does the EDC anticipate will be - will benefit most from this activity?
Thank you for the question, Council Member. Uhm, we have not done an analysis yet. This question did come up earlier and so, we said we would look into it and get back.

And does the Administration estimate the portion of the projected region of economic revenue at which actually it will be revenue that will come from this will directly flow to any of the city businesses and as far as local tax collection, any projections on that?

Uhm, so yes, as you said, $3.3 billion is the regional economic impact that’s expected. We have not done an analysis of New York City specifically. In part, because it’s just very noisy data to look at. It’s hard to see if somebody is in New York City staying at a hotel here, then they go watch a game there but they come back or someone is doing the opposite. What we do know is that people are going to be here renting hotel rooms. There’s going to be a lot of events that will be

happening. They’ll be creating you know spend across the city and then working very closely with you know across the very city agencies. NYC Tourism is going to be publishing things online where small businesses can direct people where to go etc..

Thank you. When it comes to transportation, I think this was asked a little earlier but I want to know what investments when it comes to all operational adjustments have been made to prepare New York City’s public transportation system for the anticipated surge of visitors we’re going to have to the city, and also to you know between the five boroughs and particularly to MetLife Stadium area?

Thank you Council Member. We touched on it a little bit earlier but we really understand that mass transit is going to be the way that the majority of fans reach games and move through the city and we will be encouraging the use of mass transit rather than private cars. And so, it’s two fold. It’s both ensuring that everyone can move around the city safely, you know visitors, tourists, but then also ensuring that residents face minimal disruption amidst the surge. And so, our

DOT, MTA, and kind of relevant city agencies have been working with folks on the other side of the river for the past two years both you know New Jersey Transit and Amtrak but also Port Authority, kind of the state of New Jersey and there are extensive mobility planning pieces in place. As far as moving folks to games; I have it here but uhm, there’s going to be kind of multimodal efforts, so you know traditionally there would be just the emergency transit to MetLife. We also plan, I believe, the FIFA Host Committee plans to do shuttle buses and there will be a dedicated lane that is dedicated to MTA buses, first responders and these FIFA shuttles. So, the idea is multimodal options and making sure that there is clear contingency planning for if there are issues with these options and then making sure that we have a really good communication system set up to ensure that residents, visitors, tourists understand what options are available to them early and then what options are available to them in the event of a need for a change.

And are there any projections on the revenue laws from the free

transportation or free bus service that’s being proposed during that timeframe?
We are in conversations with the governor on this fare free bus pilot and we plan to keep the Council updated as those conversations progress.

Okay, thank you, look forward to that and uhm, when it comes to the job creation, do you have any projections on job creation associated with the world cup and will any of those jobs, if any, be permanent as a result of this tournament?

So, I don’t have any projections to share in terms of jobs created. I will get back to you on that but one thing that we did want to highlight is we do see this as a long term opportunity for the city as well.
Right.

There’s going to be - tons of businesses are going to be here from across the world. We know a lot of different countries that are organizing business allegations that are going to be here. We’re talking heads of major corporations down to gross day startups to everything in between and

so, we are working very closely with those various groups that bringing those businesses here so that way we can get in front of them and pitch them that New York City is open for business. New York City is here to support them and identifying how they come to New York City, great jobs etc… So, that is one of our big focuses on how do we actually squeeze the juice out of this long term and create jobs for New Yorkers and Host.

Thank you for that. What strategies are being implemented to connect New York City residents, in particular young people and individuals from unrepresented communities to employment opportunities tied to the World Cup games?
We uh - that is obviously a priority related to the World Cup and we will have more to share on that coming soon but appreciate it.
Well, well, I mean, will there be any recruitment campaigns, actions to -

So, a lot of the work is being done in coordination with the Host Committee and so, allow us a moment to go back to the Host Committee and touch base with them and come back to you with a more thorough answer.
